title: How major US stock indexes fared Friday 11/27/2026
detail:
How major US stock indexes fared Friday 11/27/2026
The Associated Press
Fri, November 27, 2026 at 10:45 AM PST 1 min read
^GSPC
^DJI
^IXIC
^RUT

Stocks jumped and nudged Wall Street to its best week in more than a year following several days of erratic swings for influential technology companies.

The S&P 500 index rose 1.6% Friday. The benchmark index notched a 5.6% gain for the week, its biggest since April of 2025. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 591 points, or 1.2%. The Nasdaq composite rose 2.3%.

The strong finish caps an otherwise unsteady week for markets. Stocks opened with a rally on Monday, then swung sharply on Tuesday and Wednesday. Markets were closed in the U.S. on Thursday for Thanksgiving.

On Friday:

The S&P 500 rose 114.71 points, or 1.6%, to 7,297.49.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 591.99 points, or 1.2%, to 50,774.94.

The Nasdaq composite rose 543.70 points, or 2.3%, to 24,129.50.

The Russell 2000 rose 46.24 points, or 1.7%, to 2,750.30.

For the week:

The S&P 500 is up 387.10 points, or 5.6%.

The Dow is up 2,627.61 points, or 5.5%.

The Nasdaq is up 1,511.77 points, or 6.7%.

The Russell 2000 is up 168.51 points, or 6.5%.

For the year:

The S&P 500 is up 451.99 points, or 6.6%.

The Dow is up 2,711.65 points, or 5.6%.

The Nasdaq is up 887.51 points, or 3.8%.

The Russell 2000 is up 268.39 points, or 10.8%.

title: What Is The One Risk Facing Visa Stock Now?
detail:
What Is The One Risk Facing Visa Stock Now?
Trefis Team
Fri, November 27, 2026 at 11:41 AM PST 6 min read
V
^GSPC
Trade Visa on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: Anthropic Broke Its $83 IPO Price. What Did Facebook Do Next?

Visa stock closed at $424.39 on Wednesday. With dividends included, it returned 29.9% over the past year, against 8.4% for the S&P 500. It now sits 2.6% below its highest close of that year. Investors pay 34.4 times Visa's earnings over the past twelve months, while the S&P 500 trades at 21.5 times.

A price like that appears to assume Visa keeps growing much faster than the average company. For that to hold, Visa has to keep its biggest bank clients without handing much of its growth back to them. The coming year puts that to an unusual test. What is changing?

Why does the coming year test Visa's bank deals?

More of Visa's business is up for renewal than usual. On its October 27 call, management said it expected about 25% of its payments volume to come up for renewal in fiscal 2027. That is the twelve months to September 2027, and the share compares with 20% in fiscal 2026. The renewals include several large clients, and management expects a higher volume of incentives as a result. Incentives are the payments Visa makes to banks and partners under these contracts.

That cost was already rising. Client incentives grew 21% in the quarter ended September, nearly 3 points faster than in the June quarter. Management put the jump down to new deals. Net revenue grew 13.2% in the same quarter, so incentives grew faster than revenue. Every extra dollar paid to banks is a dollar that does not reach Visa's owners.

Visa's client incentives grew 21% last quarter, faster than its 13.2% rise in net revenue. If you need your savings to cover your bills, a stock whose growth is being shared with its banks is a slow source of that cash. If you count on your savings for steady income, that income has to come from other holdings. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays.

Management does not treat the extra incentives as a loss. "Remember, incentives are a tool," it said, adding that "we manage our business to drive net revenue growth." Its outlook includes the bigger renewal year. It calls for adjusted net revenue growth in the low double digits for fiscal 2027. Management also expects price increases to add about as much to growth as in fiscal 2026. Most of them take effect in the second half of the year. Even so, an analyst on the call asked why the outlook does not show more earnings growth. That leaves the question of how much of Visa the extra incentives can reach.

title: Nasdaq Leads Market Rebound as Treasury Yields Hit 5.29% at the Long End
detail:
Nasdaq Leads Market Rebound as Treasury Yields Hit 5.29% at the Long End
Nauman Khan
Fri, November 27, 2026 at 11:52 AM PST 1 min read
^TYX
^IXIC
^DJI
^GSPC

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

A rise in Treasury rates accompanied Friday's advance in U.S. equities, leaving stocks higher even as bond investors sought more yield across the curve. The move came during a holiday-shortened session.

The 30-year Treasury yield recorded the largest increase, adding four basis points to 5.29%. The 10-year rate reached 4.89% after gaining three basis points, while the two-year yield moved up two basis points to 4.66%. Rates therefore advanced across short-, medium- and long-term maturities.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with AMZN.

Is SPY fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Among equities, the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.9%, ahead of 0.5% advances in both the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500. Energy shares led sector performance. Health care lagged, although nine sectors ended higher.

Investors had few fresh economic releases to guide decisions during the session. U.S. exchanges were scheduled to close earlier than usual for Black Friday, while reduced participation following Thanksgiving shaped the trading environment. The combination of higher share prices and rising yields offered a mixed picture across financial markets as the holiday week came to an end.
